title: One regex, 27 minutes
oneLine: A new firewall rule with a runaway regex went to every server worldwide at once and pinned their CPUs.

sources.title: Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019

facts.label: Fleet
facts.quote: replicated across our more than 180 cities

facts.label: Propagation
facts.quote: 2.29s for a change to be distributed to every machine worldwide

facts.label: Peak CPU
facts.quote: spiking to nearly 100% usage across the servers in our network

facts.label: Traffic lost
facts.quote: we had lost 80% of our traffic

events.label: PR merged
events.quote: had merged a Pull Request containing the change after it was approved

events.label: Tests green
events.quote: TeamCity built the rules and ran the tests, giving it the green light

events.label: Rule deployed
events.quote: deployed a minor change to the rules for XSS detection via an automatic process

events.label: First page
events.quote: the first PagerDuty page went out indicating a fault with the WAF

events.label: WAF identified
events.quote: the WAF was identified as the component causing the problem and an attack dismissed as a possibility

events.label: Global terminate
events.quote: a team member executed the global WAF termination at 14:07

events.label: Traffic back
events.quote: traffic levels and CPU were back to expected levels worldwide

levers.label: Rollout
levers.why: WAF rules skipped staging by design
levers.quote: Changing the SOP to do staged rollouts of rules in the same manner used for other software at Cloudflare

levers.label: CPU guard
levers.why: the protection existed and had been taken out
levers.quote: Re-introduce the excessive CPU usage protection that got removed.

levers.label: Regex engine
levers.quote: Switching to either the re2 or Rust regex engine which both have run-time guarantees.

levers.label: Page to terminate
levers.why: Access was down, so engineers needed a bypass to reach internal tools
levers.quote: with our Access service down we couldn't authenticate to our internal control panel

afterwards.quote: Re-introduce the excessive CPU usage protection that got removed. (Done)
Switching to either the re2 or Rust regex engine which both have run-time guarantees. (ETA: July 31)
Changing the SOP to do staged rollouts of rules in the same manner used for other software at Cloudflare
Introduce performance profiling for all rules to the test suite. (ETA: July 19)

assumptions.what: Each staged rollout step waits 10 minutes
assumptions.why: The postmortem says staging takes hours or days. 10 minutes is the least generous reading.

assumptions.what: DOG carries no customer traffic, PIG 1%, each canary 2%
assumptions.why: The postmortem names the stages but not their traffic share.

assumptions.what: A PoP at nearly 100% CPU serves 20% of its traffic, and drops nothing below two thirds CPU
CPU climbs with a 10 s time constant and drains with a 173 s one
assumptions.why: Fitted so traffic is back within two minutes of the 14:07 terminate, as reported at 14:09. The postmortem gives no CPU curve.

assumptions.what: Detection takes 3 minutes and diagnosis keeps its share of the response in every replay
assumptions.why: 13:42 to 13:45 and 13:45 to 14:07 are the only measured human delays.
